racecards.race_name: Adam Scott Celebratory Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Yet to progress from course win in October but still has a big role to play
runners.spotlight: Yet to make any significant further progress since making all in 14-runner course maiden (2m, good to soft) on rules debut in October but wasn't beaten far when fourth of six in Newbury handicap (2m, good to soft) in February and ought to play a significant role in this.

quotes.race: Stay For The After Party 'National Hunt' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Poor Rocky [Corrigeen Rock]. We had to retire him early because he had some issues, and sadly, we got a call to say he'd broken a leg in the field.  We were all devastated about that, but Smokey [Smoke Trail] has pulled it out of the bag and he's done this for Rocky. I can't believe he's won on his first start over hurdles. Rocky started it off for us with jumps racing, and he won on his hurdle and chasing debut here. Kelso is very lucky for us and it's such a friendly course. When we bought Smokey, Lucinda said that he's very similar to Rocky. I think he'll be a chaser next year - Deborah Thomson, chair of the owners Caledonian Racing Society.

runners.owner: A Lee, J Matterson, D Mullen & Partner
runners.comment: Pulled up on hurdling debut but placed twice at big odds since; could have a say
runners.spotlight: Pulled up on hurdle debut in January but placed twice at big odds since, more recently when 80-1 third (just behind Changemyluck) in race won by 300-1 outsider here (2m, good to soft) this month; can make his presence felt again.

runners.comment: Safely held in two chases in March but consistent at a fair level over hurdles in 2025
runners.spotlight: Safely held in two chases last month but consistently showed a fair level of form over hurdles in 2025, gaining her win in Sedgefield maiden (2m4f, good) in September; big player back in this sphere; hood left off today.

runners.comment: Not beaten that far when fifth here last month but needs significant improvement today
runners.spotlight: Not beaten that far when fifth of seven here (2m5f, good to soft) last month, his second hurdle start, but looked unenthusiastic and needs significant improvement to feature today.

runners.comment: Bumper winner; ran well for a long way on hurdle debut and might come on for the outing
runners.spotlight: Delivered on earlier promise when making all in good-ground Carlisle bumper in October; behind two of today's rivals when weakening seventh on hurdle debut here (2m, good to soft) this month but ran well for a long way and wasn't beaten far; can feature if that outing brought him on.

runners.comment: Second hurdle run was much better than the first; another step forward is needed, though
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who bettered his inauspicious rules debut when 66-1 fourth at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) this month; needs to take another good step forward here, though; cheekpieces added.

runners.comment: Close second in a bumper and also showed clear promise on both hurdling starts
runners.spotlight: Close second in Newcastle bumper (good to soft) in December and displayed clear promise in two Carlisle novice hurdles (both 2m1f, good to soft) this year, albeit he was pulled up on run-in after losing his action last time; others have more compelling claims here, though.

stable_tour.quote: He was second, only beaten half a length, on his debut in a bumper at Newcastle earlier in December. That was very good and he ran a nice race. He's probably going to go straight hurdling now. You'll see him out next in the middle of January I'd imagine. 31-12-25

runners.breeder: J C Haimet, Mme E Petit, Mme H Pet
runners.comment: Tailed off when 250-1 for last month's hurdling debut at Wetherby (2m, good)
runners.spotlight: Tailed off when 250-1 for last month's hurdling debut at Wetherby (2m, good).

racecards.verdict: Smoke Trail is not opposed lightly but HERJA should benefit from this switch back to hurdling and could be the answer.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Smoke Trail, 11/4 Changemyluck, 5/1 Nobotheratall, 11/2 Herja, 9/1 Thorneylands, 10/1 Bogha Baiste, 33/1 The Grey Venture, 66/1 Melbourne Ghost, 100/1 Hashtag Queen

racecards.race_name: Malcolm "Scarra" Scott Memorial Handicap Hurdle

quotes.race: Nick Embiricos Memorial Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I think Menaggio was very good. He was a bit long at the first ditch but on the whole I was delighted with his jumping and he saw it out well. I hadn't really looked beyond this race. We just wanted to get him started. We'll sit down and have a think but he's a nice prospect and he'll get further. I think he'd get three [miles] but we're not in a rush to get there. That was a sharp as he wants there. Hopefully, he's progressing - Alan King, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He only won once over hurdles last season but his final second at Kempton was a good effort, probably his best run. He made a winning chase debut over 2m3½f at Plumpton on Monday, jumping really well and staying on powerfully. I hope he'll continue to progress, particularly over slightly further. 25-10-24

He was the first of my exciting team of novice chasers to win over fences and he did the job well at Plumpton, jumping soundly and staying on powerfully. He'd shown decent form as a hurdler and should continue to progress, particularly over slightly further than 2m4f. 07-11-24

runners.owner: G R Orchard & Mrs J M Gray

prev_owners.owner: Arf Racing, Davide Satalia & Mme Michele Juhen-Cypres

runners.comment: Close second in valuable series final here (2m5f) last month; must be considered
runners.spotlight: Yet to add to his French hurdle win in 2023 but was placed on both starts this year, more recently when close second in valuable series final here (2m5f, good to soft) last month; must be considered.

runners.comment: Off since poor run in January but was good second over C&D just after Christmas
runners.spotlight: Course winner (2m5f, good) a year ago; absent since disappointing run in January but his C&D (good to soft) second just after Christmas was a good effort and he'll be right in the thick of things if back on song today.

runners.comment: Came good at Newcastle last month, despite some poor jumping; can improve again
runners.spotlight: Came good at sixth attempt, keeping on resolutely at Newcastle (2m6f, good to soft) three weeks ago; 6lb higher here but has plenty of scope for further progress if his jumping is more fluent this time.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.comment: Back in good form lately, more notably when placed in valuable series final here (2m5f)
runners.spotlight: Returned to form with creditable third (just behind Jericoacoara) in valuable series final here (2m5f, good to soft) last month and also ran well when second in small field at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) 16 days ago; each-way claims at least.

quotes.race: Waterford FC Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan was behind the bridle the whole way, just struggling to hold his position. The trip was too short. Hugh said once he pulled him out wide he just locked onto it and once he met the rising ground he just went away from them - Eoin Doyle, trainer.

quotes.race: Dunlop Homes Rated Novice Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan was in good nick, but the only problem was the drop back in trip. Slower ground out there helped and he handles it no problem - Hugh Morgan, rider.

quotes.race: Dunmore East Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Rauzan wasn't really suited by Winter ground. His jumping has come together and I think there is a bit of improvement in him. He could do a job on the Flat over a trip - Eoin Doyle, rider

runners.comment: Bounced back in new blinkers with creditable third in series final at Musselburgh in March
runners.spotlight: 4-12 over hurdles (including C&D win); out of sorts when pulled up twice in the winter (wore cheekpieces) but bounced back with creditable third in valuable series final at Musselburgh (3m, good to soft; first-time blinkers) last month and has possibilities if in the right mood again.

runners.comment: Not at best lately but won twice here in the autumn and is back on a good mark
runners.spotlight: Dual course winner (2m2f/2m5f) in the autumn; not in same form lately and untested over this far but back on a good mark and can't be ruled out.

runners.comment: Won this off 1lb higher in 2025 but more consistent rivals appeal more
runners.spotlight: Now 1lb lower than when winning this race in 2025 (good ground) but fell in a chase last month and dropped out of contention rather tamely when back over hurdles here (2m5f, good; breathing issue reported) 18 days ago; might be aided by refitted tongue-tie but more consistent rivals appeal more.

quotes.race: Betting.Bet Betting Maiden Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I wanted to get the stands' rail on the run-in, so I thought I'd better go for it approaching the last before the leader shut the door on me. Dollar Collar is still a bit weak but toughed it out - Stephen Mulqueen, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Kept on for second behind Jehol De Thaix on last month's handicap debut; cheekpieces on
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 5yo who kept on for clear second behind Jehol De Thaix on last month's handicap debut at Newcastle (2m6f, good to soft); big player if first-time cheekpieces prompt any further progress.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Cab On Target Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I love racing because of the horses and Starlyte is the sort of horse I love. She's only tiny but she's so brave. You have to drop her in and let her pass horses and I'm delighted for the owners Allan and Anne Grant who've just got married - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Thehawkponteland On Instagram Mares' Handicap Hurdle (Go North Lady Buttons Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Starlyte needs a fast-run two-and-a-half miles and she's the most game horse. It's her attitude that wins her races - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She came to us from the Flat and made a flying start by winning a 2m4½f Newcastle handicap hurdle. We'll keep her to that trip with a view to going up to 3m later. She desperately needs good ground and is ready to go as soon as things dry out. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Absent since poor run in November and tends to save his best for Cartmel now
runners.spotlight: Won here in 2023 but probably better known as a Cartmel regular now (gained last two wins there); off since a poor run in November and might be of greater interest when back at Cartmel and with this outing behind him.

quotes.race: Racing Again Sunday 13th November Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Secret Secret was as tough as nails and he can't go far enough. They went very quick and I told Dylan he was a keen horse and not to be worried about how far he got out of his ground. In this grade on that ground it would only be a matter of staying going. He just gallops, that's his forte - Emmet Mullins, trainer

stable_tour.quote: We bought him at the sales in the summer and I quite liked the look of him but he didn't have the best of reputations, so he only cost £1,500. We thought we'd try to have some fun with him and he's been a little revelation - it's great to still be able to buy a cheap horse and win races. He won at Cartmel on his first start for us and then bolted up at Kelso. We ran him on ground too soft back there last time. He'll have a campaign through the spring and summer, maybe starting off at Perth and then doing the Cartmel tour. 14-02-24

racecards.verdict: The suggestion is JEHOL DE THAIX who opened his account at Newcastle three weeks ago, despite a sketchy round of jumping.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Jehol De Thaix, 5/1 Jericoacoara, 7/1 Rauzan,  Starlyte, 15/2 Nosy Neighbour, 8/1 Magic Wave, 10/1 Menaggio,  Kilmore Rock,  Heart Above, 16/1 Secret Secret, 25/1 Dollar Collar

racecards.race_name: Royal Caledonian Hunt Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Not beaten far when last of four over C&D in February; still unexposed over fences
runners.spotlight: Dual course winner over hurdles; finished alone in a match race on seasonal/chase debut in October then wasn't beaten far when last of four over C&D (good to soft) in February; eased in grade today and could still have potential over fences.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: That was a good performance. Old Gregorian got a lot of confidence from his last win and he'll be better again when he steps up to two and a half miles. He jumps hurdles quickly and well - Alan Doyle, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: Who knows if he'd have still won at Wetherby on his chasing debut if his rival hadn't unseated, but his jumping was very slick. He definitely wants two and a half miles and will improve going up in trip. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Without a win since 2024 but consistent for new stable since December; in the mix again
runners.spotlight: Yet to add to his four chase wins for Philip Kirby during 2023-24 season but has made the frame on all four starts for current stable since December, most recently when third of five at Newcastle (2m4f, good) nine days ago; tried in cheekpieces today; probably won't be far away.

quotes.race: Vickers.Bet Independent Family Owned Bookmaker Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Special Rate jumped brilliant. I let him run to the front down the back, I thought he'll stay anyway and he's kept galloping - Ross Chapman, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.breeder: Scea Haras Des Evees & Mr Daniel Cherdo
runners.comment: Landed good prize in January but is not the force of old; others appeal more
runners.spotlight: Made all to land good prize at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) in January and is also very well suited by this track but he's no longer the force of old and was unable to land a telling blow at Carlisle last month; others have more appealing profiles.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Auld Reekie Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We ran Breizh River in a novice hurdle first just to get his confidence up and then he ran well at Newcastle last time in a race that's got a bit of form in it. The only thing we were worried about today was he's never had a good race at Musselburgh before, but he was well at home, so we thought we'd try. We'll wait and see what we do next. We'll get him back home and keep him happy. His jumping was fantastic - Tristran Davidson, trainer.

quotes.race: Ray & Anita Green Chasing 500 Winners Handicap Chase (Registered As The Simply Ned) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Breizh River is a cracking horse. He's been very lightly raced and we're just going to target him at certain races throughout the season. He won't take a lot of racing because he's only six and is quite backward in his mind, but he's obviously very tough. He'll have a break now and we'll aim him at the Southam Handicap Chase over two and a half miles at Cheltenham's November meeting. That was always the plan and we know he wants further - Paul Robson, trainer.

runners.owner: Mrs Suzy Brown & Peter R Brown
runners.comment: Yet to build upon pleasing reappearance run in October and needs to up his game
runners.spotlight: Won off today's mark at Hexham (2m4f, good to soft; first-time visor) towards end of last season but is yet to build upon his pleasing reappearance run in October and needs to up his game.

quotes.race: Schloss Roxburghe Hotel Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jet Legs had no weight on his back and a good 5lb claimer. He's a nice horse for the future. He's a laid-back character, a good traveller through the race. His owners have been very patient, you'll see the best of him as a staying chaser; Martin Todhunter, trainer.

runners.comment: Largely consistent 10yo; off since October but ran well when fresh last spring; a possible
runners.spotlight: Largely consistent 10yo who belatedly opened his chasing account at Perth (2m, good; first-time cheekpieces) last summer; absent since below-par effort in October but ran well when fresh here (2m4f, good) last spring and returns from latest break on a workable mark.

runners.comment: 0-6 over fences but creditable third in valuable C&D series final last month; big player
runners.spotlight: 0-6 over fences but gave very good account when third in valuable series final over C&D (good to soft; first-time cheekpieces) last month and has been dropped 1lb since; big player if new headgear continues to help.

stable_tour.quote: He won a Wexford bumper and was fourth over hurdles at Punchestown. He was bought to go chasing but should have a productive season as a hurdler. He's a big, strong horse who'll improve with time and hasn't shown his best yet. He has a very likeable attitude. 16-10-24

runners.comment: Won by 11l over C&D on recent chase debut; 9lb higher in higher-grade race today
runners.spotlight: Returned from break with career-best performance this month, drawing clear to win by 11l over C&D (good) on chasing debut; 9lb higher in a higher-grade race today but could easily have more to offer over fences.

quotes.race: Colin Hawkins (Jockey) Memorial Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We had a couple of entries in this race and were keen to run something. Carrigeen Castle looks a progressive horse. He'll probably have one more run then we'll look forward to next season with him - Micky Hammond, trainer.

runners.comment: Safely held on last month's chasing debut but that came after a long absence
runners.spotlight: Safely held on last month's chasing debut at Ludlow (2m4f, good) but that came after a 489-day absence and she's well handicapped on old hurdling form; no surprise if she gets closer to the target today.

stable_tour.quote: She was a decent bumper mare last season and made a successful hurdling debut at Huntingdon last week. She was a little green but won well in the end and I think she'll appreciate slightly easier ground. 25-10-23

She was a decent bumper mare last season and has already made a successful start over hurdles, winning at Huntingdon last month. She was a little green but did it well in the end. She'll appreciate slightly easier ground. 10-11-23

racecards.verdict: The verdict goes to SPECIAL RATE, who scores good marks for consistency and might be aided by new headgear.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Looking Splendid, 5/1 Old Gregorian,  Joecooker, 11/2 Special Rate,  Carrigeen Castle, 9/1 Garde Des Champs, 10/1 Breizh River,  Kay Tara Tara, 16/1 Jet Legs

racecards.race_name: Reg And Betty Tweedie Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Made all in new blinkers over C&D in November but pulled up three times since; now visored
runners.spotlight: Made all in first-time blinkers over C&D (good to soft) in November, his third course win, but was pulled up on all three subsequent outings and needs switch to first-time visor to provoke another resurgence.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes 'Best Odds Guaranteed On Racing' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dropping back down in class helped him. He's a nice little horse. I feel sorry for Patrick on Your Own Story but Cadell probably had a little more toe on the day - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Novices' Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Cadell is a horse we've always liked and we'd been looking forward to him stepping up to three miles over fences. He won two point-to-points and this was always going to be his game. You just dream that he'll eventually turn into a Scottish Grand National type, he likes good ground and stays very well. We're a long way off things like that but they have to be in the back of your mind, you can dream - Michael Scudamore, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's another nice staying chaser. We probably put him in at the deep end a couple of times the season before last, when he perhaps physically wasn't quite ready. His race was over at the second fence at Kelso on Saturday as his saddle slipped, but he'll still be aimed at the Borders National. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Ran well for a long way at Doncaster last time but this 11yo has become inconsistent
runners.spotlight: Ran well for a long way when fourth at Doncaster (3m, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) in February and remains well handicapped but this steadily regressive 11yo has become inconsistent, and others appeal more.

quotes.race: Download The Racing AppHandicap Chase
quotes.quote: Erne River obviously likes Doncaster. He lost his way a bit but Nick Kent has his horses in good form - Charlie Hammond, rider.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We knew Erne River was a very good horse and his two wins last season were a bonus as I didn't think he'd be quick enough for hurdle races. He oozes chasing and I was really pleased with that - Nick Kent, trainer.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie La Grugerie Et Al
runners.comment: Below form on latest outing but is 2-7 for new stable this season and enters calculations
runners.spotlight: 2-7 for new stable since the autumn, the latter win gained by just over 8l at Carlisle (3m, good to soft) last month; below form when back at Carlisle a fortnight later but still considered.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV This Christmas Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Hudson De Grugy is a great horse, and hopefully that can get his confidence back up going forward. We've always really liked him, but he's very ground dependent. He just needs to get going again - Sam England, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Daily Multiples Offer At Cheltenham Novices' Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was well deserved. That is the first time Hudson De Grugy has had his ground this season. The ground is definitely key to him. We have been dry for so long we could be destined for a wet April which I would be more than happy with as he could come back here on the final day of the season for the Josh Gifford memorial race. Hopefully we will get another run in between. Two and a half miles is probably about his distance but he would probably stay three miles if we didn't ride him so aggressively. He has got a big heart - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Kingston Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: "I didn't want him to make the running today with that weight on his back. Andrew Cooper will be delighted hasn't got any smashed hurdles like he did last time he was here. He's maturing and the better ground seems to suit. I thought it was a stiff task. He'll come back for the handicap hurdle here on Tingle Creek day."-Gary Moore, trainer

quotes.race: Paddy's Giving Away £1 Million Today Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I saw the wood coming past me three out and it was just a bad decision of mine. I thought if he winged it that would put the race to bed, but he wanted another stride. He's a big, strong horse and all he does is gallop. He's got a lot of scope but he's not the most natural over hurdles, so we have to school him a lot. I think he's more of a chaser than anything - Josh Moore, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: His jumping let him down a bit last season and he could just do with brushing up on that. He'll probably start in a handicap chase at Sandown on November 10. He wants heavy ground and anything from two and a half to three miles. 28-10-25

He's come from Gary and Josh Moore and is a horse for chases over 2m4f and upwards, hopefully one for the better races on Saturdays. He's rated 120 and he's won off 123 over fences in the past. He's obviously dipped, hence they sold him, but we hope to get him back to his old form. He was ready to run three weeks ago but needs some rain. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Didn't run badly when fifth here (3m2f) last month and has become well handicapped
runners.spotlight: Not really firing on all cylinders since scrambling home by a neck on seasonal debut at Carlisle (3m, good) in October but now 6lb below that mark, and didn't run badly when last of five finishers here (3m2f, good to soft) in March; had another wind op (his third) soon after that latest outing; one to consider.

quotes.race: Vesta Wealth Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dare To Shout thought he'd won the race after the last, but then they all came to him. To his credit, he stuck his neck out again. We always thought he'd stay three miles and, if anything, he's enjoyed the better ground today - Danny McMenamin, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Gordon Richards Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dare To Shout is not a big horse but I like the way he jumps as he's neat. He'll appreciate soft ground and three miles better - Ian Hamilton, owner.

quotes.race: Johnston Smillie Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: DARE TO SHOUT is a nice little horse. He did the job well and he'll jump a fence one day. Ian Hamilton speaking to Racing TV.

runners.breeder: S C E A Du Haras Des Sablonnets Et Al
runners.comment: Won three in a row in February/March 2025 but this is his first run since
runners.spotlight: In excellent form in February/March 2025, winning three in a row at around 3m (good to soft/good), but has fitness to prove after 393-day absence and will need to hit the ground running to have any chance off current mark.

quotes.race: Ladbrokes Go North Red Rum Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Red Happy is quirky, he has a think about it at the start, but he's been a star for us and that's five races he's won for the yard. We're limited because he's a lot better right-handed. We had him in at Kelso but we were forced to come here - Jonathan Bewley, jockey.

quotes.race: Secret Garden And Gd's Pooley Bridge Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Red Happy has done well for us all right. We got him from David Pipe the week after he won his last race for him, and we couldn't be happier that he's stayed in good form. It helps a lot when you get a horse who can keep going like he does. He toughed that out and didn't miss a single jump ? he jumped for fun when they were out in the country. We'll keep him on the go and see what the handicapper does - George Bewley, trainer.

runners.comment: Four wins last season (two here) but largely disappointing since; has a point to prove
runners.spotlight: Last season's chasing four-timer included two course wins (2m1f/2m5f) but he's been disappointing since, barring a keeping-on second at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) in December; pulled up in Carlisle series final won by Wolfburg last month, and moves back up in trip with questions to answer.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Best Odds Daily Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Going an extra half mile in trip really put Walk On Quest back into his comfort zone. He'd won twice over two miles and he just looked like an out-and-out stayer every time he won - Alan Doyle, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He was second in his point-to-point and seems like a good horse. He's pleased us at home and reminds me of Giovinco. He's only four and we don't do particularly well with bumper horses, but he's one to follow over a period of time as he's working well. 15-11-23

prev_owners.owner: G R Orchard And Annie Mania

runners.comment: Won series final by 9l at Carlisle last month and is now 2-5 over fences; respected
runners.spotlight: Readily drew clear to win valuable series final by 9l at Carlisle (2m4f, good to soft) last month and is now 2-5 over fences; went up 11lb for that but could have untapped potential over this longer trip; respected.

quotes.race: Racing Post+ Subscription Go North Monet's Garden Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Wolfburg's been a different horse since he's gone chasing. This is easily the best day of the season. It's all just come together. It's been a brilliant weekend, winning a bumper as well with King Kubala, who's going to be a proper horse. We've had a rough season, for lots of reasons. The horses haven't been quite right but things are going well now. - Sandy Thomson, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Racing Bet Builder Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Wolfburg showed a bit of form as a young horse then fell away. They've had some things done to him, his wind and stuff like that, and cheekpieces and fences seemed to help him. On the whole his jumping was very good - Craig Nicol, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He came back from his last run at Carlisle with a bit of an injury, so he's had some time off. He'll be back in work shortly and we'll keep him hurdling now. He needs a bit of time between his races. He was good in a bumper and very good the day he won over hurdles at Catterick last season and you can probably give him excuses for some of his other runs, which have been disappointing. He'll be a cracking novice chaser next season. 22-01-25

racecards.verdict: The one with least to prove is WOLFBURG (nap) who looked in particularly good nick when winning over 2m4f at Carlisle last month.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Wolfburg, 4/1 Erne River, 11/2 Dare To Shout, 7/1 Hudson De Grugy, 15/2 Red Happy, 12/1 Cadell,  Walk On Quest

racecards.race_name: Scottish Racing Academy Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners.comment: Pulled up on both outings this year, after a long layoff; cheekpieces added today
runners.spotlight: Still has low mileage and will be suited by today's forecast good ground but, following a long absence, has been pulled up on both outings this year; needs a good boost from the new cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 out of form but resumes on a good mark and has fairly good record when fresh
runners.spotlight: Absent since ending 2025 with two disappointing efforts but resumes on a good mark and has fairly good record when fresh; could be dangerous if first-time visor has desired effect.

stable_tour.quote: She's out of Legacy Gold, who won the Listed mares' bumper at the Grand National meeting for Stuart Crawford and was a good hurdler, and she jumped very well when winning a point-to-point at Bartlemy by ten lengths. She's been bought by Michael Scholey and will go straight over hurdles - the £50,000 mares' novice handicap at Kelso in the spring could be a target. 16-10-24

prev_owners.owner: Mrs S Russell & A M Russell

runners.comment: Showed only minor promise in novice/maiden hurdles but was useful on the Flat; interesting
runners.spotlight: Showed only minor promise in three novice/maiden hurdles (1m7f-2m) last September-November but was useful on the Flat in his prime and may yet transfer more of that ability to this code; wears first-time tongue-tie for handicap hurdle debut; market may guide.

runners.comment: Unplaced all four starts for new stable this season; others look safer
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two respectable efforts at Carlisle (2m1f/2m3f, soft) but was soundly beaten there on latest outing in February (raced too freely) and has now been unplaced all four starts for current stable; sports refitted hood and first-time tongue-tie here; others look safer.

runners.comment: 0-8 over hurdles but ran big race at Carlisle this month; player if judged on that
runners.spotlight: 0-8 over hurdles and has rather mixed record this season but ran big race in defeat at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) 16 days ago and has obvious claims if in the right mood again here.

runners.comment: Absent since breakthrough win in February 2025 but remains very lightly raced
runners.spotlight: Very lightly raced 8yo who returned from a layoff to open account at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) in February 2025; not seen since but may still have potential and can evidently go well when fresh.

stable_tour.quote: He ran well in a bumper in May last year when he was fourth despite being as green as grass. His half-brother [Sir Valentino] was third in the Champion Chase [in 2017]. He'll be going straight over hurdles. 25-10-23

runners.comment: Disappointing 7yo who has been soundly beaten in three chases this year; now back hurdling
runners.spotlight: Disappointing 7yo who has been soundly beaten in three chases this year and now reverts to hurdling; usual cheekpieces left off today; needs to turn a corner.

runners.comment: Fair Flat racer; pulled up when returned to hurdling for stable debut in January; risky
runners.spotlight: Fair Flat racer who won a juvenile event on hurdling debut in 2023 but was not seen again over jumps until pulled up in Catterick handicap on stable debut in January; current ability in this sphere remains hard to gauge.

quotes.race: Savills Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Gozo is a nice horse and is so gifted and he knows it but he always just does enough. He'll school big and bold first time then he'll go low so I said to Dad I thought this would just be like a schooling session for him and someone must've heard it because he got backed off the boards. We'll probably give him another run, he idled rather than got tired there, but he'd probably go to Musselburgh - Ben Brookhouse, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He had a small setback after his Plumpton win, where he idled late on having gone from the front. We were going to run him in the Triumph Hurdle trial at Cheltenham ithis month but he'll probably be back out early next year. He can dominate small fields but whether he's good enough to be competitive in the big leagues remains to be seen. There's a chance we could send him to the US in late spring to try to pick up some prize-money over hurdles and potentially sell him on. 30-11-23

runners.comment: 0-7 over hurdles but could plausibly have been perked up by recent stable switch
runners.spotlight: 0-22 on the Flat and 0-7 over hurdles; sold out of Matt Crawley's stable for 3,400gns after well-held fourth at Fakenham (2m, soft) in February but ought to be better suited by the forecast faster ground here, and could plausibly have been perked up by her new regime.

runners.comment: Pulled up on last month's handicap debut, having refused to settle; blinkers discarded
runners.spotlight: Unexposed after only five hurdle runs but was pulled up on last month's handicap debut, having refused to settle; might be more relaxed without blinkers (worn for last three races) here but still looks too risky.

runners.comment: Kept on steadily for never-dangerous fourth on handicap debut, and still has potential
runners.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who is likely to have entered a few notebooks after last month's handicap debut at Wetherby (2m, good to soft), where he kept on steadily from the rear for a never-dangerous fourth; moves up in trip here; watch the betting.

racecards.verdict: It's worth chancing the fitness of low-mileage 8yo THE BEST WAY, who is only 2lb higher than when winning after a layoff last February.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Big Love, 7/2 The Best Way, 9/2 Gonnino, 11/2 Struth, 8/1 Parisian Fashion, 12/1 Alvesta, 16/1 Interchangeable,  Ozzy Cosmo,  Gozo, 33/1 Ellistrin Bay, 66/1 Highly Recommended

racecards.race_name: Scottish Racing Academy Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners.comment: Good-ground bumper winner who has made the frame on all of her three starts over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Good-ground bumper winner who has made the frame on all of her three starts over hurdles; steps up in trip on her handicap debut and should give a good account provided she shows improvement.

quotes.race: Join Us On New Year's Day 'Junior' Open NH Flat Race (Go North Jodami Series Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Conner [McCann] is fantastic on the bumper horses and we use him a lot on them claiming 7lb. Hunters Spring was in training as a two-year-old for the Flat but she was too backward and not ready for it. The owners understood she would have a better chance being given a bit of time and going for junior bumpers and it's really paid off. She looked very professional, she quickened nicely and was given a very well-judged ride - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

runners.comment: Placed in five of his eight runs over hurdles without looking particularly progressive.
runners.spotlight: Placed in five of his eight runs over hurdles without looking particularly progressive; in good heart though and looks sure to win a race such as this; place claims at least.

runners.comment: Won a bumper here last April; has shown ability in three runs over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Won a bumper here last April; has shown ability in three runs over hurdles and can be expected to show improvement now that he steps up in trip on his handicap debut.

stable_tour.quote: All is good with him. He was entered at Newcastle on Friday but I didn't want to take a chance on fast ground as most of the family seem to prefer it a bit softer. There's a juvenile bumper at Wetherby on the first Saturday in December and he might well appear there. He's done a lot of jumping and it's not impossible he could go straight over hurdles for the National Hunt three-year-old hurdler series. I don't know if he's another Elvis Mail in the making but Ginger Mail wasn't either and he's progressed to a mark of 126. The family improves and I'd love to think this chap could be the same. He's got a bit of speed about him but he's quite weak. I won't be overracing him this season. 21-11-24

runners.comment: Won over hurdles at Musselburgh in December off 6lb lower; placed three times since.
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish; got off the mark over hurdles at Musselburgh (1m7f, soft) in December off 6lb lower; placed three times since, running up to his best when second of 11 finishers at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month; should be thereabouts.

runners.comment: Pulled up when 80-1 on handicap debut at Hexham last month.
runners.spotlight: 0-8 under rules; pulled up when 80-1 on handicap debut at Hexham (2m, soft) last month; easy to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: Ran as if he needed the run when fourth at Sedgefield 19 days ago after eight months off.
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark over hurdles at Kempton last April off 2lb higher when trained by Nigel Hawke; ran as if he needed the run when fourth of six finishers at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) 19 days ago on his stable debut after eight months off; sports first-time cheekpieces and has to be of interest.

runners.comment: Jumping was less than fluent when beaten 52l at Newcastle last month.
runners.spotlight: 0-9 under rules; jumping was less than fluent when beaten 52l at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) last month; can do better in time.

runners.comment: Just modest form in two runs over hurdles; steps up in trip on handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Just modest form in two runs over hurdles; steps up in trip on handicap debut and no surprise if she shows considerable improvement for a good yard.

runners.comment: She has offered little in three runs for current yard and it's easy to look elsewhere.
runners.spotlight: Sole success over hurdles came in January 2024 when trained by Archie Watson; she has offered little in three runs for current yard and it's easy to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: Yet to make the frame in four starts over hurdles but has time on his side.
runners.spotlight: 1m Flat winner in September 2024 when trained by the Kublers; yet to make the frame in four starts over hurdles but has time on his side; hood worn on last two starts is left off; may do better at some point.

racecards.verdict: The one to be interested in here is FINE POINT who won for his previous stable off 2lb higher last April. The danger is Newport.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Rememberthename,  Fine Point, 100/30 Ms Cindy Kate, 11/2 Newport, 15/2 Lester Mail, 8/1 Hunters Spring, 16/1 Miss Friday Lions,  Glenridding, 33/1 Barrakilla Vage, 50/1 Chosen Hero

racecards.race_name: Church House Investments Buccleuch Cup (A Maiden Hunters' Chase) (Corinthian Spirit Qualifier)

runners.comment: Fourth in this last year but not at best in points this season; new cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Dual point winner; gave good account when fourth (just behind Theoldboggroad) in this race a year ago but has not been at his best in points this season and needs help from the new cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Ran well in two maiden points last month but others look stronger here
runners.spotlight: Maiden pointer who was pulled up in 2024 edition of this race on only previous rules start; ran well in two 2m4f maiden points last month (albeit ran out at final fence on first occasion) but others look stronger.

runners.comment: 2-4 in Irish points and 4-5 in British points; likely contender on rules debut
runners.spotlight: 2-4 in Irish points in 2025 and 4-5 in British points for new connections this year, the latest win gained in three-runner contest this month; seems versatile regarding ground and is a likely contender on rules debut.

runners.comment: Maiden point winner; about 12l behind Boley Bob when third on latest outing
runners.spotlight: Made all to fend off The Back Braes in maiden point at Friars Haugh (3m, good to soft) last month, his fifth attempt, but was about 12l behind Boley Bob when third at Tranwell (3m, good to soft) three weeks later; further progress required.

runners.comment: Easy winner of conditions point at Overton last month; makes rules debut today
runners.spotlight: Two point wins this year, the latter gained easily by 16l in Overton conditions race (2m4f, good) last month; ought to make his presence felt on rules debut.

runners.comment: Returned from long absence with point second last month and might come on for the run
runners.spotlight: 0-7 under all codes but returned from long layoff with close/clear second behind Flying Skipper in Friars Haugh point (3m, good to soft) for new trainer last month, and has possibilities here if that run brought him on.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs A Maclay & Mrs E Innes

runners.comment: Placed in this race in 2025, and returns here after open point win last month; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Third in this race last year, his only start under rules, and returns here after winning an open point at Overton (3m, good) last month; shortlisted.

runners.comment: Dual point winner this year; again ran well when second to Boley Bob at Tranwell last time
runners.spotlight: Began year with two point wins at Alnwick (maiden/restricted) and again ran well when second (beaten about 4l) behind Boley Bob at Tranwell (3m, good to soft) last month; each-way claims at least.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list in this historic hunter chase is BOLEY BOB, who makes his rules debut after four consecutive point wins.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/5 Boley Bob, 4/1 Phantoms Cave, 14/1 Theoldboggroad, 20/1 Amma Lord,  Bentley Road,  High On The Hill, 25/1 The Back Braes, 33/1 Flying Skipper

racecards.race_name: Racing TV Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: Mrs A L Merry & Mr Brett Merry
runners.comment: 9-1, made a winning debut in 12-runner bumper at Newcastle last month.
runners.spotlight: 9-1, made a winning debut in 12-runner bumper at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month, overcoming greenness to get up on the post; saddled with a 7lb penalty but has more to offer for yard with fine bumper record this year; player.

runners.comment: Beaten 4l when fourth behind Midday Rendezvous at Newcastle last month when favourite.
runners.spotlight: Beaten 4l when fourth behind Midday Rendezvous at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month when favourite; looks sure to improve and must come into the reckoning.

runners.comment: Fifth behind Midday Rendezvous at Newcastle last month.
runners.spotlight: Winning pointer; fifth behind Midday Rendezvous at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month; wasn't beaten far and any significant improvement should see him bang there.

runners.comment: Yard not renowned for their exploits in bumpers and he's likely to need more time.
runners.spotlight: Second foal; dam once-raced sister to bumper winner Nana Joan, half-sister to bumper and 2m-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Glencassley, out of 2m/2m3f hurdle winning half-sister to Velka Pardubicka winner Registana; yard not renowned for their exploits in bumpers and he's likely to need more time.

runners.comment: Unlikely to be seen at her best until she steps up in trip over hurdles.
runners.spotlight: Sixth foal; half-sister to winners Fenland Tiger (2m4f-3m2f hurdle/chase) and Teescomponentstrig (3m hurdle); dam placed bumper/2m5f hurdle, half-sister to bumper winner Seren Rouge, out of 1m3f Flat and useful 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase winner; pedigree is laden with stamina and unlikely to be seen at her best until she steps up in trip over hurdles.

runners.comment: Turned in a creditable effort when runner-up on his debut at Wetherby last month.
runners.spotlight: Turned in a creditable effort when runner-up on his debut at Wetherby (2m, good) last month; difficult to gauge what that form is worth but he should be competitive.

racecards.verdict: There may be more to come from Newcastle winner MIDDAY RENDEZVOUS and he can remain ahead of Dilrisk, who is second choice.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Dilrisk, 5/2 Midday Rendezvous, 7/2 Eagle Warrior, 9/2 Cape Warrior, 25/1 Yorgunnarock, 50/1 Teescomponents Gal

racecards.race_name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners.comment: Scored at Southwell in January and continued in good form; ought to be in the shake-up
runners.spotlight: Scored at Southwell (7f) in January and he's continued in good form, doing best of the pacesetters when third of 14 in 1m Yarmouth handicap nine days ago; he ought to be in the shake-up again in refitted cheekpieces.

runners.comment: Not best placed when 15th at Doncaster last time; needs considering off a slipping mark
runners.spotlight: Landed 1m2f amateurs' handicap at Newbury last summer and in better form than his recent form figures suggests, not best placed when 15th in 1m Doncaster handicap last time; needs considering off a slipping mark.

quotes.race: Grosvenor Sport New Customers Double Odds Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
quotes.quote: Alazwar is a great horse to have. We bought him as an unraced horse from Shadwell many moons ago and he's just kept producing. He's Brodie's [Hampson, jockey] favourite and I'm delighted with him. These races are hard enough to win. It's easy if you dip in and out of them, but if you're trying to target them like we are with a small group, then you need horses who are going to be consistent - Archie Watson, trainer.

quotes.race: Thoroughbred Industry Employee Awards Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
quotes.quote: Alazwar has been knocking on the door and running very consistently in these amateur races. He's Brodie's favourite horse, so it means a lot to her. He's proved himself very versatile when it comes to trip this year and he's great for these kind of races - Archie Watson, trainer.

quotes.race: Extra Places Any Day With Betfair Handicap
quotes.quote: Alazwar is a lovely horse who's quite progressive on his day - when he's good he's good. I was surprised he handled ground so quick, but he bounced off it. The mile was perfect for him - Hollie Doyle, jockey.

quotes.race: Racing TV "Junior" National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Alazwar is a gorgeous horse that has always shown a lot of class at home. I've not had much to do with him and Brodie (Hampson) has been in charge throughout his training. He has done that very well in the manner of a good horse. Gavin Sheehan said he was very professional. I don't think he will benefit from running in another of those under a penalty so all being well he will go straight to the Listed Bumper at Cheltenham on New Year's Day - Archie Watson, trainer.

runners.comment: Ended time for Iain Jardine with Newcastle win; more needed for new yard off 4lb higher
runners.spotlight: In excellent form for Iain Jardine this winter, signing off with 1m Newcastle win in February; more is needed for his new yard off a 4lb higher mark.

runners.comment: In excellent form on AW this winter; only ninth at Nottingham latest but can bounce back
runners.spotlight: In excellent form for her new yard on the AW this winter, scoring over C&D and at Kempton (1m); only ninth back on turf in 1m Nottingham handicap last time but no surprise to see her bounce back here.

runners.comment: Largely in good nick this term; not ruled out off a 2lb lower mark here
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with victory at Wolverhampton (8.5f) in December and largely in good nick this term, a close fifth in 8.5f Wolverhampton handicap two weeks ago; not ruled out off a 2lb lower mark.

runners.comment: Off four months before solid Kempton fourth latest; can go very well with Simon Walker up
runners.spotlight: Back to winning ways over C&D in November and resumed from four months off with a solid fourth of nine in 1m Kempton handicap 19 days ago; he can go very well with that run under his belt with Simon Walker up.

runners.comment: Off since a below-par C&D seventh in August 2024; has his fitness to prove for new yard
runners.spotlight: Scored over C&D but signed off for Stan Moore with a below-par C&D seventh later in August 2024; off the track since and has his fitness to prove on his yard debut/comeback run.

stable_tour.quote: He's very well handicapped. He had run three lovely races on the all-weather and then everything went wrong at Bath. You have to put a line through that because he near enough pulled up. He ran really green at Newbury when he was fifth but was finishing fast over seven furlongs. He was very raw, he had a bit of a leg in every county, but he's just a slow learner. He's probably a miler but could get ten furlongs. He's out of a very good Pivotal mare and he's massive. He's 17 hands, so he'll probably end up being a far better four-year-old than a three-year-old. He'll be one to follow for the second half of the season. 04-07-24

prev_owners.owner: HP Racing King Of The Dance

runners.comment: C&D scorer; good second in 7f handicap here latest; must enter calculations off same mark
runners.spotlight: C&D scorer who comes here on the back of a good second of nine in 7f handicap here 26 days ago; must enter calculations off the same mark.

stable_tour.quote: He ran once last year when an encouraging third over 6f at Windsor. He had a few issues after that, hence why he didn't run again until last month when finishing in mid-division at Lingfield. He was ring rusty but has come on in leaps and bounds since and the plan will be for another novice to get a handicap mark - he could be a dark horse for later in the season. 03-08-22

runners.comment: Yet to register a victory but she ended 2025 in good nick; has gone well off a break too
runners.spotlight: Yet to register a victory but she ended 2025 in good nick, second of 13 in 9.5f Wolverhampton in October; she has gone well off a break too so needs considering.

runners.comment: Caught eye for new yard when second at Doncaster latest; very much one to consider
runners.spotlight: A fair 1m winner for Noel Meade in 2025 who caught the eye for his new yard when a running-on second of 22 in 1m amateurs' handicap at Doncaster 22 days ago; very much one to consider.

quotes.race: Racing Again Saturday, May 10th Apprentice Handicap
quotes.quote: Noel (Meade) told me Port Louis can be quirky and keen, and I didn't want to interfere with him too much. I gave him a little rein, didn't touch off his mouth, and it worked out lovely as we went a good pace - Wayne Hassett, jockey speaking to RacingTV.

racecards.verdict: C&D winner CHICO DULCE (nap) made an encouraging return from a break when fourth at Kempton and gets the vote with Simon Walker up.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 No Knee Never, 4/1 Chico Dulce, 6/1 Rosemary's Rose, 13/2 Showmedemoney, 7/1 Little She, 10/1 King Of The Dance,  Port Louis, 12/1 Alazwar,  Tam Lin, 14/1 King Of Speed, 33/1 Snooker McCrew, 40/1 Thursday

racecards.race_name: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap

runners.comment: Below best on soft in October but good 6f turf winner previously and has won over 6f on AW
runners.spotlight: Below best on soft in October and gelded since; had looked suited by the stiff 6f at Salisbury when winning there previously and although he won over this trip on his Kempton AW debut last spring, today's sharp test may be on the inadequate side; still has some potential, though.

runners.breeder: Mme Isabelle Mauger & Mr Guy Benachour
runners.comment: Five AW wins elsewhere over 6f/5f; fair run latest but not obviously ahead of his mark
runners.spotlight: Can lead; five AW wins at 6f and 5f; has settled into a handicapping groove since the latest of them in February and although he wasn't far away under Harry Vigors at Wolverhampton (6f; blinkers replaced cheekpieces) 11 days ago he isn't obviously ahead of his mark.

runners.breeder: Airlie Stud & Mrs S M Rogers
runners.owner: Mrs J Woods And K Lawrence
runners.comment: Ran well in sole 6f AW run; won 3 of first 4 turf runs in 2025; near latest winning mark
runners.spotlight: Ran well at Kempton in sole 6f AW run (as 2yo) but proved a far better 3yo, winning three of his first four turf starts, over 6f and 7f; his form deserted him later but he returns to action only just above his latest winning mark last June; interesting.

quotes.race: Conundrum HR Consulting Handicap
quotes.quote: Rare Change threatened in nurseries last year to take himself to the next level and he's done that. He needed to today. We were markedly up in grade but did it really well. I thought it was very close but I was in the right place - Hector Crouch, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We've always held him in high regard and he ran a blinder at Glorious Goodwood when third in a 6f nursery. Oisin Murphy felt he may have ridden him wrong on the day but he competed well in a very good nursery. He was only sixth at Doncaster last Friday, so he's frustrating, but talented, and we're going to have to figure out how to win with him. 18-09-24

prev_owners.owner: Michael Iavarone & Julia Iavarone & Michael O'Callaghan

runners.comment: Rather mixed in 2025 but pick of 6f form on turf/AW gives him good claims at the weights
runners.spotlight: Smart in his prime; not the same force now but the pick of his 6f form on turf and AW in 2025 suggests he's well treated if the race happens to fall his way and this is an easier grade than he often tackles.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Abergwaun Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: It's a very sharp five at Tipperary, hence the headgear, but it kept Twilight Jet concentrated. We'd lots of dreams and aspirations after he won the Lacken but  he was very sick after Ascot, then had colic surgery since and later slipped on a hard surface so needed surgery on his hock. This year was race to race so and he had a good blow afterwards. The headgear may stay on. He could go to Newbury or further afield in the coming months and may stay in training - Michael O'Callaghan, trainer.

quotes.race: Goffs Lacken Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Twilight Jet doesn't know when to stop. He's a very good horse. He's as tough. He got better and quicker with every run. He went to the Breeders Cup and that might have been one race too many for him. He's come back bigger and stronger this year and even quicker I think. He's the real deal - Leigh Roche, jockey.

quotes.race: Newmarket Academy Godolphin Beacon Project Cornwallis Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: The plan was to make the running but we got a nice lead into it and the race couldn't have gone any better. Twilight Jet has plenty of speed and handled the drop back to five. He liked this ground but is quite versatile in that regard - Leigh Roche, rider.

runners.owner: Ged Mason, Sir Alex Ferguson, Jim McGoff
runners.comment: Wide-margin AW winner over 6f on reappearance as 3yo; useful turf form in the autumn
runners.spotlight: Has gone well fresh, having run well in sole 2yo start and a wide-margin winner on Wolverhampton AW (6f; made all) on reappearance last year; put up a bold show against the older horses in a competitive 6f race at Nottingham in October and looks a likely type for this race.

racecards.verdict: Rare Change and HOODIE HOO were both quick out of the blocks in 2025 and the latter is only narrowly preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 Hoodie Hoo, 9/4 Dyrholaey, 100/30 Dr Strangelove, 6/1 Rare Change, 8/1 Twilight Jet

racecards.race_name: Joan Butcher 90th Birthday Fillies' Handicap

runners.owner: Hasmonean Racing, C Fahy And Marchants
runners.comment: Wide-margin winner of handicap debut at Wolverhampton (1m1f); solid run since; new trip
runners.spotlight: Improved for the switch to a handicap when seizing the initiative early for a wide-margin AW win at Wolverhampton (about 1m1f) in January; couldn't pull off a 6lb rise against a course specialist there last month but she still gave it plenty and this new trip is plausible on pedigree.

runners.comment: Two Wolverhampton wins at 1m and 1m1f; stays 1m4f there; run only once in last 12 months
runners.spotlight: Two Wolverhampton wins (about 1m and 1m1f) last midwinter; no sign of her flagging when a strong-finishing third over 1m4f there in October, in only her second attempt at the trip; however, that was her sole run in the last 12 months so there are some readiness queries; cheekpieces refitted.

runners.comment: Won back-to-back 1m4f races on turf last summer; ready success over C&D in December
runners.spotlight: Well beaten over inadequate 1m on comeback last year but she came into her own when upped to 1m4f in the summer, winning back-to-back turf races; had seemed rather becalmed after but she won nicely over C&D when last seen in December; should be further openings for her off 2lb higher.

runners.comment: Lightly raced; found plenty when leading near the line at Kempton (1m4f) last time; up 4lb
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who finished remote on return from nearly a year off at Kempton last month but she was all the better for the run, and the fitting of a hood, when finding the most to lead near the line at Kempton (1m4f) 12 days ago; back up 4lb in a higher grade but capable of more.

prev_owners.owner: The Turf Club & Mrs Harry Dunlop

runners.comment: Three 1m4f wins last year; just hung on for C&D success in January; needs best form to win
runners.spotlight: Tough mare who added three more wins at about 1m4f last year and made a successful return to the AW when clinging on in an amateur jockeys' race over C&D in February; faded into third after making the running at Wolverhampton since and needs best form to win today.

quotes.race: Fitzdares Telephone And Text Betting Handicap
quotes.quote: Sea Of Charm isn't the easiest to win with so it's good to get her head in front. I thought we might be vulnerable at the two [furlong pole] but she pulled out a bit more - Tom Marquand, jockey.

runners.comment: Won off this mark and higher on turf (1m4f) in 2025; only just failed on Tapeta latest
runners.spotlight: Two of three turf wins at about this trip in 2025 came off today's mark and higher; pleasing start for new yard over 1m at Southwell last month and she was slightly checked in her run when only just losing out there (1m3f) 18 days ago; interesting weights chance.

quotes.race: DragonBet Proud Sponsors Of Chepstow Racecourse Handicap
quotes.quote: Phaedra is very straightforward, so it just made sense to go forward and see what happened. As it turned out, I was in front, and nobody wanted to take me on - Sean Levey, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.spotlight: C&D winner last April but that remains her sole win and she's mostly struggled at both sprint trips this year; looks up against it.

quotes.race: Watch On Racing TV Handicap
quotes.quote: The Gay Blade is not a bad little horse at his level. He likes it around the likes of Hamilton and Musselburgh and is pretty consistent - Iain Jardine, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a good horse for our racing club and gives everybody a lot of fun. He has his level but you can set your clock by him when he's in his grade. He seems to like Hamilton and he battled on gamely to dead-heat there last week - he got carried over the track and I think he ought to have been given the race. Although he handles an all-weather surface he's more effective on slow ground on turf. He could do well on wet ground at the back end. 26-07-24

runners.comment: Has been kept busy and won twice at Wolverhampton (6f) last month; hampered latest

quotes.race: Remembering Frank Hugill Handicap
quotes.quote: We're delighted - and Quercus probably did it easier than he's ever done before there. He's only won once elsewhere and he just seems to come alive around the track. The winningmost horse there has nine wins, so we'll be eager to try and get him to ten wins there now - Ann Duffield, trainer.

quotes.quote: Quercus just loves it here. The track suits him and while we call him 'quirky quirk' at home, he's actually really genuine. There was another race for him on the card, but this looked easier and it was worth it. There's a race here next week which looks like it'll be for him, so we'll be back then - Ann Duffield, trainer.

runners.comment: Has five wins on AW; losing run is mounting up but slipping down weights.
runners.spotlight: Five AW wins but losing run is mounting up; needs a fast pace to aim at and is slipping down the weights; likely to come good again one of these days.

runners.comment: Sole success came over C&D in September 2024 off 5lb higher mark; has deteriorated since.

quotes.race: Trustatrader Apply Today EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I took a bit of a gamble and ran World Of Darcy at Newmarket over seven furlongs because I felt that now's the time to decide what we're going to do with him. Luke [Morris, jockey] said drop him back to six and get him a bit of confidence because he's obviously had a few hard days at work and we picked this one. There's nothing wrong with him, but he's not very big. There's always going to be a doubt whether this horse trains on, but at the moment he eats well and works well. There's a winter campaign and I think that's what I'm aiming for. We've got a big entry at the weekend, but we'll look at that and decide what the ground does. We'll see how he recovers and then we'll make decisions - John Ryan, trainer.

quotes.race: Racehorse Lotto National Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: World Of Darcy is a good solid horse, he'll be winning plenty of races. He'll probably go for the Windsor Castle - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Northern Commercials - Used Stock For Quick Delivery EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: I was very impressed. World Of Darcy travelled really sweetly and I could have done with a lead for longer. Karl said whatever he did today that he would improve a lot for it - Sam James, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He was second to Elite Status, who's a very good horse, in the National Stakes and will definitely go for the Windsor Castle, barring accidents. He's tough and solid and the stiff five furlongs will play to his strengths. He'll go there with a chance. 14-06-23

runners.comment: C&D winner on his penultimate run and he's in the mix back in trip after short break

runners.comment: Solid fourth on handicap debut at Catterick and has claims if he can build on that

runners.comment: Unexposed colt who was eye-catching fourth on handicap debut at Wolverhampton; dangerous
runners.spotlight: Didn't show a great deal in three 2yo runs but he started his handicap career with a strong-finishing fourth at Wolverhampton (5f, Tapeta) last month; that was eye-catching from off the pace and he should benefit from that run; shortlisted.

runners.comment: 0-7 but he's finished a close third in last two starts including over C&D; key player
runners.spotlight: 0-7 but he went close in a C&D handicap last month and backed that up with another creditable third at Southwell (5f) last time; on unchanged mark and he's a big player if this sets up for his closing style.

runners.comment: Went close at Southwell on penultimate run and has claims if she can recapture that form

runners.comment: Still unexposed and mark is falling but she needs more on AW debut
runners.spotlight: Five-race maiden who has not progressed so far and was disappointing when favourite on her Catterick reappearance (5f handicap) 12 days ago; still unexposed and mark is falling but she needs more on AW debut.

quotes.race: Sky Sports Racing Sky 415 Handicap
quotes.quote: Call Me Betty is a model of consistency and good placing by the boss [Michael Dods, trainer] to get her back out. She was even better today as she had no one pestering her and she put the race to bed from two [furlongs] down - Connor Beasley, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Won in good style over C&D last time and he's a big player again off 4lb higher
runners.spotlight: 4yo who recorded his third win when beating ten rivals over C&D last month; back up 4lb but he travelled strongly for a long way last time and hit a personal best with that stylish success; key player.

runners.comment: On dangerous mark and was runner-up over C&D on his penultimate run; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Seven-time winner who scored off 1lb higher over C&D in September; has been hit and miss since but he finished second here (7f) on his penultimate run and wasn't disgraced after an awkward start at Southwell last time; usually races prominently and he's not ruled out back at this track.

runners.comment: Sole win was at Ripon last April but he's run plenty of good races since; in the mix
runners.spotlight: Sole win was at Ripon last April but he's run plenty of good races since, including when fourth over C&D last month; continues to edge down the weights and he shouldn't be far away.

runners.owner: The Dalby Family And P Kirby
runners.comment: His last three wins have been at Newcastle and he went close here last time; interesting
runners.spotlight: His last three wins have been at Newcastle and he produced a powerful finish when going close in a Class 4 here (6f) last month; looks interesting off only 1lb higher on this drop back in grade and his last success was over C&D.

quotes.race: Clean Up With PPS Handicap
quotes.quote: The Green Man did that easily enough and he's in good order with himself, he hasn't moved as well as this in a long time. He's flourishing. He's a big horse and he's just fully maturing - Joseph Parr, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: The penny really dropped for him this winter over 7f on the all-weather and he was kept very busy, winning twice and being placed a number of times at Newcastle. He's having a well-earned break now and we'll probably aim to bring him back around August for a late turf campaign and then back on the all-weather in the winter. 23-04-25

runners.comment: Three wins over C&D during the winter and he had an excuse here latest; not out of it

runners.comment: 11-time course winner but he was only sixth behind Anthropologist over C&D last time
runners.spotlight: 11-time course winner who defied this mark over C&D in December; some creditable efforts since but he has been a bit up and down and was only sixth behind Anthropologist here last time; others preferred.

stable_tour.quote: He's a superstar for the stable, who was bred by my mum and dad. He ran last Friday, not beaten far at Southwell under Jack Sullivan and will now have a summer break. With 16 all-weather wins under his belt, he's a stable favourite and is as enthusiastic as ever. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Won over C&D last month and wasn't far behind Anthropologist here last time; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Record of 2-20 but his last win was over C&D last month and he was only beaten 2l behind Anthropologist here last time; remains feasibly treated on his best form and he has possibilities.

quotes.race: Jumps Free Trial At racingtv.com/freetrial Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Prolific winner but he's not threatened here in his last two starts; needs to raise game
runners.spotlight: Prolific winner who is generally reliable but he's not threatened in his last two starts, the latest behind Anthropologist over C&D last month; continues to edge down the weights but this is a deep race and he needs to raise his game.

stable_tour.quote: A tough and consistent horse who'll go to the Western meeting for a 7f handicap. The owner lives near Ayr, so it would be lovely if he were to get his head in front. He just doesn't want the ground too soft. 10-09-25

runners.comment: Course specialist but last win was 13 months ago and he has a bit to prove after a break

runners.comment: On last winning mark but she returns from eight months off and others are preferred
runners.spotlight: Scored off this mark over C&D last March but she didn't hit the same level in seven subsequent runs last year; has a bit to prove after eight months off and regular hood is missing on this step back up in grade.

quotes.race: talkSPORT Powered By Fans Handicap
quotes.quote: Too Much has done it nicely and hopefully she can progress. I don't think she's going to be a superstar but she's honest and tries hard so hopefully we can get another couple of numbers out of her - PJ McDonald, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Both wins were in 2024 and this looks tough back up in trip and grade; down the list

runners.spotlight: Improved upon her 6f maiden/novice form to win at 16-1 on nursery debut at Newcastle (1m, AW) in December; bred to do better still and returns to action with her trainer among the winners; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: Won on final 2yo start and pedigree provides optimism that he has more to offer
runners.spotlight: Improved to win at 11-2 at Leicester (7f, soft) last October on his second nursery start; gelded since; he's on quicker ground for this reappearance but his pedigree provides optimism that he has more to offer.

runners.comment: Still didn't appear to be the finished article when 7-2 runner-up on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Struggled towards end of last year on first three starts but gelded subsequently and was an entirely different proposition when 7-2 runner-up on handicap debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) four weeks ago; still didn't appear to be the finished article and is open to further improvement; turf debut.

stable_tour.quote: He was unlucky on his handicap debut the other day and slightly surprised us. He never really showed much in novices and is a big, raw animal who's just going to keep progressing as he steps up in trip. 02-04-26

runners.comment: Returns from absence but the new trip could suit on handicap debut; monitor the betting

runners.comment: Hasn't been running badly this year but 0-9 and needs something extra today
runners.spotlight: She's dropped down the weights and hasn't run badly on her two starts this year (7f, AW); however, she's 0-9 and needs something extra on this first crack at 1m.

runners.comment: Kept on well for third over 6f on handicap debut and every chance that 1m is within range
runners.spotlight: Kept on well for close third of 14 at 14-1 on handicap debut at Pontefract (6f, good to soft) recently, behind two who got first run; there's every chance that 1m will be within range and she could be in the mix.

runners.comment: Just one win from her 15 starts but that was over C&D when 3lb higher; not ruled out

runners.spotlight: There are winners in her pedigree and she makes her handicap debut off a basement mark; a market check is advised but she's achieved little across her four races and improvement is necessary.

runners.spotlight: Well beaten last October when last seen but on heavy ground; prior to that he was a close fourth over C&D and this lightly raced 5yo reappears with his trainer (who runs two) among the winners; could be involved.

runners.comment: 9yo who is on a competitive mark but was below par on his latest outing in January

runners.spotlight: 0-6 over 7f but has frequently hinted at 6f that this trip will suit, as when keeping on for 2l fourth at Catterick (good) on recent reappearance; she has a solid record here and could be thereabouts.

quotes.race: Racing TV Handicap
quotes.quote: I had to be patient today to get the gap, but once it opened One Of Our Own picked up well and put her head down. I kept it simple, but she's an honest filly who tries. It's nice to get her head in front today - Kaiya Fraser, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.quote: My lad races lazily but when I started to get after Without Exception after the second-last he seemed to be picking up and picking up. Philip (Rothwell) said ride him wide and I did, it worked out anyway. The ground at Down Royal last time was too quick, these conditions suited - Tiernan Power Roche, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: Jumped badly at Limerick last time when failing to back up a Thurles win
runners.spotlight: Belatedly off the mark at Thurles in February in an amateur handicap chase (soft-to-heavy), winning going away on only his third run over fences; more needed to confirm that form but possible.

quotes.race: BOYLE Sports (Q.R.) Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Rideau Canal had promised a lot, but that was a very long time coming. He was a bit non-committal about everything, so I jumped him over banks and ditches hoping to ignite his enthusiasm, which I think it did. I wasn't expecting this but he was very good, and I'm delighted for his owner Jules Sigler who also won with Westandtogether at Navan recently. Georgie gave him a gorgeous ride and when I was doing my Gordon Elliott gig, she won the Ladies Derby in the Curragh, so she has sort-of ridden for me! She is well able to ride and did exactly what was needed to be done today - Denise Foster, trainer.

runners.comment: Flopped when well fancied for a handicap hurdle last time, has won twice at this venue
runners.spotlight: 3-34 over fences, with two of those successes coming at this track, including when 33-1 chance in this race in 2023; creditable third in a 2m7f handicap chase here on New Year's Day; flopped when well fancied for a handicap hurdle at Limerick last time.

runners.comment: Hard to win with, fair run on stable debut at this venue, not as good at Thurles last time
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-18 over fences; lost his form for Philip Rothwell last summer but fair effort on yard debut at this venue on New Year's Day; not as good at Thurles last time.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Another Ocana seems to save his best for Limerick as he had some good runs here before. He handles that ground and it's great to get the job done today. He hit the line strong - Eoin Walsh, rider.

runners.comment: Second reserve, in good form over hurdles, backed up Down Royal win with Limerick second

runners.comment: Won at Thurles in January, form of Gowran third advertised in the Aintree Foxhunter
runners.spotlight: 2-12 in points; improved from Limerick run at Christmas when a 25-1 winner of a maiden hunter chase at Thurles in January; handled heavy conditions well, and did well to recover from a bad mistake at the seventh; third in the Tetratema at Gowran last time, winner Let's Go Champ franked the form with Aintree Foxhunter third.

quotes.race: Racing Again February 5th Maiden Hunters Chase
quotes.quote: We definitely expected Cold Old Fire to be placed but obviously the favourite fell and it opened up a bit that way. We fancied him to run a big race and we were hoping to finish second so we're delighted with him. He's a small little horse but is as tough as nails and jumps out of the stable raring to go every morning. He goes on heavy ground and Darragh won on him a couple of times in point-to-points. He gallops and stays and it's always great to get a winner on the track. - Raymond Hurley, trainer.

runners.comment: Looked promising when beating a decent yardstick at Clonmel, sustained progress is likely
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt in point-to-points for Cormac Doyle at Ballingarry (3m, good) last May; made a bright start for Willie and Patrick Mullins when beating Magic Sadler (winner of nine points) in a maiden hunter chase at Clonmel in January; 7lb claimer takes over now on a youngster expected to mature into a top-class performer in this category.

quotes.race: Rathronan Maiden Hunters Chase
quotes.quote: I Walked The Line is brilliant to jump and we finished a long way clear of the third. We've been trying to replace Billaway and I had Cause For Comment last year, who didn't quite measure up, so I got this horse. I'm hoping to make him into a Billaway-type horse. Being by Walk In The Park attracted me. He's up for sale to stay in the yard - Patrick Mullins, jockey.

runners.comment: Won gamely at Cork with the two market leaders filling the places, stronger opposition now
runners.spotlight: Only one win from ten starts in points; now on the upgrade; good run in defeat against West Of Idaho at Tyrella before a remote third in a hunter chase at Downpatrick; came good at Cork at fortnight ago, winning gamely with the two market leaders filling the places; stronger opposition now.

quotes.race: John Thomas McNamara Series Maiden Hunters Chase
quotes.quote: We hummed and hawed about coming here, thinking it was a bit quick after Lawful Ruler was third last week in Downpatrick. But he likes the better ground and he was very well during the week. He was at the beach and in the water and was jumping and ate up and everything so we said we would come and take our chance. We'll think about it and maybe if he got a handicap mark we could go for one - Paul Stafford, trainer.

runners.comment: Sprang a 33-1 shock in this race last year, likely to be available at big odds again
runners.spotlight: Veteran with modest strike rate in points (1-19); sprang a 33-1 shock in this race last year; likely to be available at big odds again; out of the money in his last two starts in points.
